title: How much longer is the Danio than the Goby?
description: Two tiny fish are written in tenths and taken away from each other to find the difference in their lengths. Keeko then asks how big the fish are compared to a finger.
teaching_notes: One idea: a length below one unit and a length above one unit are both written in tenths before the shorter is taken from the longer. Ask each child to hold a ruler along a finger and say how the fish compare.

source: A Celestial Pearl Danio is 2 4/10 cm long and a Philippine Goby is 9/10 cm long. What is the difference in their lengths? How big are these fish compared to your finger?
video_script.why: The child has taken one length from another by breaking a unit and now does it for a length below one unit by writing both in tenths.
video_script.substitution: Write both lengths as counts of tenths, take the shorter from the longer, then change the tenths back to units and tenths.
video_script.anchor: A Celestial Pearl Danio and a Philippine Goby drawn side by side above a centimetre scale
video_script.payoff_line: The difference in their lengths is one and five tenths centimetres
never_show: a length in centimetres for a finger
maths_rules: The Danio is a little more than 2 cm and the Goby is less than 1 cm, so both are small beside a finger. No finger length is given.
video_script.design: One idea: write both lengths in tenths, take the shorter from the longer, and change back to units and tenths. Assumes the child can change units and tenths to tenths. The real-life beat is the book's own question about a finger. The two fish stay all video.
open_questions: The worklist step gives a finger length of 6 to 8 cm, but the book text does not, so the video does not say it.

<bookmark mark='take'/>Both lengths can be written as counts of tenths. Then we take the shorter length from the longer one.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the Danio is two and four tenths centimetres, and the Goby is nine tenths of a centimetre.

beats.on_screen: To find: the difference in their lengths

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, write both lengths in tenths. Two and four tenths is twenty four tenths, and the goby is already nine tenths.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, take the shorter length from the longer one. Twenty four tenths take away nine tenths leaves fifteen tenths.

marks.back: 10/10 turns into 1 cm and 5/10 cm remains

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, change back to units, because fifteen tenths is ten tenths and five tenths.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Ten tenths make one centimetre, so we have one centimetre and five tenths.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The difference in their lengths is one and five tenths centimetres.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
